## What this notebook checks

Keep biological sex and gender as distinct variables and state exactly how
each is coded. Identify categories with few observations. Define the average
associations and interaction tests, which assess whether an association
changes across another variable or group. Define the groups of \(p\)-values
adjusted together and use separate output names for near-eye and chest
analyses.

## What this notebook uses and produces

- Uses: the prepared H10 dataset in `artifacts/06_model_data/H10.rds`.
- Produces: definitions and sample counts for the age, sex, and gender
  variables; fitted models; model checks; adjusted estimates in interpretable
  units with 95% confidence intervals. Participant-day models report
  participants, participant-days (model observations), and sites;
  participant-level models report participants (model observations) and sites.
  Sex and gender category counts are reported overall and by site so sparse
  cells remain visible. Tables, figures, and source data are retained.
- Fixed rule: near-eye and chest results are saved under different names and
  cannot overwrite each other.
- Data sensitivity: fit this identical H10 implementation to the
  manuscript-prepared dataset and compare exact samples, sex and gender cell
  counts, estimates, 95% confidence intervals, diagnostics, and conclusions.
- Formula display: the completed audit must contain a visible evaluated code
  cell printing the exact Wilkinson formulas passed to the selected model and
  every fitted comparison model.
